title: Sandbox Hosts
description: Host-level view: fleet size and scaling, per-worker capacity and which pool binds, worker failure rates, the boot → capacity-advertised critical path, and release/process health. Per-host series arrive through the gateway's /metrics/hosts federation, which relabels every worker series with host="<id>".

panels.title: Live workers
panels.description: Workers seen within the heartbeat TTL. Includes resumed standby workers that sit outside the MIG target, so it can legitimately exceed it.

panels.title: Provider target
panels.description: The MIG's own target worker count, polled by the gateway (the sole MIG writer). Absent rather than zero when the provider poll has never succeeded.

panels.title: Draining
panels.description: Workers cordoned for scale-in: still serving what they hold, accepting no new placements. One that stays cordoned is capacity being paid for and not used.

panels.title: Release-gated workers
panels.description: Live workers excluded from placement because their release is not the expected one. Non-zero mid-rollout is normal; non-zero afterwards is a half-deployed fleet.

panels.title: Not golden-ready
panels.description: Live workers without a staged golden snapshot. They cold-boot every create instead of cloning, and a still-warming worker advertises slots_free=0 by design.

panels.title: Unscrapable workers
panels.description: Live workers the gateway could not scrape for /metrics/hosts. Their per-host panels below go blank while the sandboxes on them keep running.

panels.title: Workers: live vs provider target
panels.description: Heartbeat-live against the MIG target and the gateway's grow-only scale-out watermark. The watermark re-baselines to the live count when the queue empties, so it can read below the fleet's real size — it is diagnostic, not a scale-in floor.

panels.title: Fleet capacity vs demand
panels.description: Placement trusts host-reported `slots_free`, never total − used: a warming worker reports zero free while running nothing, and a big-memory sandbox eats several slots' worth. Demand converts committed memory into default-slot equivalents.

panels.title: Scaling actions
panels.description: Scale-out requests the gateway submitted to the provider, and the cordon → drain → delete-by-name path on the way down. cordons − removed − aborted should equal the draining count; delete failures leave a host cordoned and are retried.

panels.title: Worker capacity
panels.description: Gateway's placement-eye view of each live worker: what it has, what it is using, what it will accept now, and how many ready VMs a create could claim instantly. Sorted by used slots — the top row is where the load is.

panels.title: Slot utilization by worker
panels.description: Used over total slots. Bin-packing means the fullest eligible worker is picked first, so a spread of values is expected, not a balance problem.

panels.title: Memory admission by worker
panels.description: Committed guest memory (each sandbox's effective mem_mib + 156 MiB VMM overhead) over the host's budget. This is the check that returns 503 on create AND on wake, and it bounds slots_free.

panels.title: Binding pool by worker
panels.description: Which pool actually limits this worker: taps and IPs are held by running sandboxes (so hibernation releases them), ports are held by explicit mappings and stay reserved through hibernation — which makes the port pool the ceiling on TOTAL sandboxes, not running ones.

panels.title: Allocatable slots by worker
panels.description: Host-reported free capacity per worker. A worker sitting at zero while running nothing is warming (golden build) or gated, not full.

panels.title: Create concurrency saturation
panels.description: Bring-ups holding a create-concurrency slot, over the per-host ceiling. At 1.0 a burst is queueing in-process — which is the point: it stops a boot storm from turning into fleet-wide agent-readiness timeouts.

panels.title: Inventory by worker
panels.description: User-visible running sandboxes per worker, stacked to fleet total.

panels.title: Hibernated by worker
panels.description: Frozen inventory per worker. It holds no slot and no memory but its artifacts and host port live on that worker's disk, which is what makes scale-in a drain rather than a delete.

panels.title: Ready pool by worker
panels.description: Ready VMs available versus builds still gating. A worker that never reaches its target pool size is failing builds — see the failure panel.

panels.title: Worker failure rates (events/min)
panels.description: Failures attributable to a host rather than to load. A single worker producing all the create errors is the signature of a host-local defect — the jailer io.max/device class of bug that once took a worker out of service while it still advertised capacity.

panels.title: Unflushed billing evidence by worker
panels.description: Closed billable intervals still only on this worker's disk. A cordoned worker with a backlog must not be deleted — the bucket, not SQLite, is the billing record.

panels.title: Guest memory touched by worker
panels.description: Sum of the VMM cgroup charges on each worker: what the host is really paying for its guests, as opposed to what admission charged.

panels.title: Committed vs budgeted memory by worker
panels.description: The admission ceiling and how close each worker is to it. Dashed budget lines that differ across workers mean mixed SLOTS_PER_HOST or MEM_PER_SLOT_MIB — check the deploy, not the load.

panels.title: Rootfs allocation by worker
panels.description: Per-VM rootfs blocks on each worker's data disk, including extents still shared with the reflinked golden base. Growth is real consumption; the level is inflated by counting that base once per sandbox.

panels.title: Guest CPU by worker
panels.description: Consumed CPU seconds per second (credited at interval close) against allocated vCPU-seconds. The ratio is the oversubscription each worker is actually running.

panels.title: Guest network by worker
panels.description: Guest-perspective throughput per worker; also where NAT egress is being paid from.

panels.title: Boot to capacity: the autoscale critical path
Slowest worker: boot → capacity
panels.description: Worst `sandbox_worker_ready_seconds` in the selection: GCE reporting RUNNING to advertising usable capacity. This — not the resize call — is what a burst waits on.

panels.title: Readiness by worker
panels.description: Per-worker boot → capacity_advertised. A worker that adopted a baked golden data disk lands far below one that had to cold-build it.

panels.title: Boot phase offsets
panels.description: Each stage's offset from the boot anchor, contributed by three writers that cannot share memory (startup script, Nomad task run.sh, serve itself). `capacity_advertised` — not `first_heartbeat_ok` — is the moment new capacity is real: an unwarmed host heartbeats slots_free=0 on purpose.

panels.title: Readiness over time
panels.description: Readiness of each worker as the fleet scales. These are absolute timestamps rather than rates, so the ordinary scrape interval still recovers millisecond boundaries — no special scrape needed for profiling.

panels.title: Worker health gates
panels.description: Per-worker gates: scrapable, golden staged, and whether the boot timeline belongs to this boot (a suspended-then-resumed standby keeps its original timeline, which is correct — it re-ran neither the startup script nor serve).

panels.title: Worker releases present
panels.description: Distinct release SHAs running across the fleet. Anything but 1 means a rollout is in flight or stalled.

panels.title: Gateway / expected worker release
panels.description: The gateway's own release and the worker release it gates placement on. The gateway is deployed FIRST by design — new gateway in front of old workers is the benign direction.

panels.title: Youngest worker uptime
panels.description: Time since the youngest worker's serve process started. A repeatedly resetting value is a crash-looping task, which reconcile makes safe but not free: it kills orphaned VMs and clears their rows.

panels.title: Guest telemetry failures (5m)
panels.description: Utilization ticks where a running guest did not answer /stats, fleet-wide. Concentrated on one worker it is a host problem; spread evenly it is an image-pinned agent predating the endpoint.

panels.title: Worker release presence
panels.description: Which release each worker is running, over time. This is the panel that shows a half-deployed fleet, the failure mode that once passed a REST smoke test while the interactive shell was broken everywhere.

panels.title: Worker process uptime
panels.description: Per-worker serve uptime. A step down without a rollout is a restart; shutdown hibernates rather than destroys, so sandboxes survive it.

options.content:
**Federation, not service discovery.** Prometheus scrapes only the gateway. The gateway holds each
live worker's address and token, scrapes their `/metrics`, and re-exports every series with
`host="<id>"` — so `job="sandbox-hosts"` series are worker-sourced, and `job="sandbox-gateway"` series
are the gateway's own aggregates. The dynamic MIG needs no SD config. `sandbox_host_scrape_ok{host}`
flags a worker the gateway could not reach; its panels go blank while its sandboxes keep running.

**Two capacity vocabularies, on purpose.** `sandbox_host_slots_*` (gateway) is the placement view:
what it will actually reserve against. `sandbox_pool_*` / `sandbox_committed_mem_mib` (worker) is the
mechanism: which pool binds and how close admission is to its ceiling. Placement trusts host-reported
`slots_free`; total − used overstates capacity when big-memory sandboxes are running.

**The worker scrape is slower (30 s) than the gateway's (5 s)** because it fans out to every worker.
Per-host panels are therefore coarser than the fleet ones — don't read a 5 s spike off them.

**A burst that is not getting hosts** → *Fleet size and scaling*. Queued demand with a flat provider
target means scale-out is not firing; a rising target with flat live workers means hosts are booting.
Continue in *Boot to capacity* — that span, not the resize, is the latency.

**A worker that will not take creates** → *Per-worker capacity*. Zero allocatable with zero running is
warming or release-gated (check the two stats up top), not full. Otherwise read the binding-pool
bargauge: taps/IPs bound running sandboxes, ports bound running + hibernated.

**One worker producing all the errors** → *Per-worker inventory and failures*. Host-local defects look
exactly like this while the host still advertises capacity.

**Before deleting a cordoned worker** → check its unflushed billing evidence and hibernated inventory.
Both live on that instance's disk.

**Sandbox-side symptoms** (slow creates, starved guests, disk full, missing usage) belong on **Sandbox
Workload**; public ingress, TLS and raw port leases stay on **Sandbox Fleet**.
